description.content: USD virtual cards a business issues to its own customers, funded and spent through your API. In test mode the whole lifecycle is real in shape and nothing is real in money: no PAN is issued, no issuer is contacted, and no test balance can become spendable. A live key is answered leg by leg rather than with one blanket refusal, because the rails are not all missing at the same rate. Listing, retrieval, freeze and unfreeze run live today — freeze and unfreeze ask the issuer first and only then move our own record, so an issuer that refuses leaves the card active and answers `503 service_unavailable`. Issuing, funding, withdrawal, close, spend limits and the transaction list each answer `403 live_precondition_unmet` and name the rail they are waiting on in `error.param`: `cardholder`, `funding`, `withdrawal`, `settlement`, `limit_format` or `transaction_sync`. A `param` of `provider` is about your card row, not a rail: that live row carries no issuer id, or an issuer this server has no card code for. The authorization simulator stays test-only under every key — a live authorization is decided by the issuer, not by us. No live leg moves money yet.

Issues one sandbox USD card to one of your customers. The card starts at `balance: 0` with
no spend limits, and every later call on this surface moves or gates that balance.

`customer.first_name`, `customer.last_name` and `customer.email` are required; the customer
is validated and then **not stored** — no name or email is persisted on the card, so a
leaked card id carries no PII with it. `reference` is yours, unique per business (a repeat
returns `409 duplicate_reference`), and defaults to the card id. `currency` may only be
`USD`; sending anything else returns 400.

The three limits are optional at issue time and are set or cleared later on
`POST /cards/{id}/spend_limits`. They are per-card ceilings you choose, and no platform maximum
is applied to any single axis. FirstFlip's ceilings sit elsewhere: one on how many cards a key
may hold open, and one on what all your cards may spend together — both stated below and in
the authorization section.

FirstFlip's one cap on issuing is a count, not an amount: a key may hold **250 open cards**.
The 251st `POST /cards` answers `409 card_limit_reached` with `param: cards` and nothing moves;
closing a card frees a slot, so a healthy integration is never locked out. Resending the same
`Idempotency-Key` is not a new card and is not counted.

The response shows `number_last4`, `expiry_month` and `expiry_year`. Those are minted here
for shape only — this card has no issuer, no full PAN and no CVV, and `sandbox.real_card`
says so on every answer. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Live mode: a live key is refused here before the body is read — issuing a real card needs the
cardholder rail FirstFlip has not built, so this answers `403 live_precondition_unmet` with
`param: cardholder`. No card is minted, and the refusal is what your key replays.

Sets the merchant-side ceilings an authorization is judged against. Send at least one of
`daily_limit`, `per_transaction_limit` or `monthly_limit`; the axes you leave out are left
alone, and an explicit `null` clears that axis (no ceiling).

`daily_limit` and `monthly_limit` are rolling windows — 24 hours and 30 days from now, not a
calendar day or month — and they are summed from the **committed** approvals at the moment the
spend lands, not from a read taken earlier. That is what makes the ceiling hold when thirty
authorizations arrive at once. `per_transaction_limit` is a single-authorization maximum and is
checked before either window. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Live mode: refused — the issuer has rejected every amount format this platform has tried on that
call, and a ceiling sent in the wrong unit is worse than none. Writing it only on our side would be
a limit a live card does not actually obey, so this answers `403 live_precondition_unmet` with
`param: limit_format`.

description.content:
The stand-in for a live purchase, and the only way to see an approval or a decline on this
surface. An **approved** authorization is the debit: the ledger row (`type: authorization`,
`status: approved`) and the balance drop commit together. A **declined** one writes the row
with `status: declined` and a `decline_code`, and moves no money.

The decline reason is decided in this order: `card_frozen`, `over_per_transaction_limit`,
`over_daily_limit`, `over_monthly_limit`, `over_tenant_monthly_limit`, `insufficient_funds`.
Code your retry logic against those six — a frozen card and an over-limit card are different
customer conversations, and `insufficient_funds` is the one a top-up fixes.
`over_tenant_monthly_limit` is the only one of the six that is not yours to set: it is a
ceiling FirstFlip places on what all of your cards may spend in a rolling 30 days
(**$1,000,000** of approved authorization spend per business).

Every answer is `201`: a decline is a recorded outcome of a real request, not a failed one.
A closed card is the exception and answers `409 card_closed`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key`
header — the same key cannot approve and decline two different attempts.

Live mode: refused with `403 live_mode_unavailable`, and this is the one leg that will stay that way.

info.name: FirstFlip API (v1)
info.description:
# FirstFlip API — start here

Accept crypto and get paid in your own currency. This collection is the whole API in **test mode**:
nothing here moves real money.

## Five steps to a paid test charge

1. **Pick the environment.** Top right, choose **FirstFlip Sandbox**.
2. **Paste your test key.** Open the collection's **Variables** tab and set `secretKey` to your
   `ffk_test_…` key (during the beta, FirstFlip issues it on request over a private channel).
   Keep it secret; never share a screenshot of it.
3. **Account → Retrieve the account for this key.** Press **Send**. You should see your business name
   and `"livemode": false`.
4. **Charges → Create a charge.** Press **Send**. You get a charge with a crypto amount and a
   `hosted_url`. The charge id is saved for you automatically.
5. **Sandbox → Simulate a payment**, then **Charges → Retrieve a charge**: the status is now `paid`.
   If FirstFlip registered a webhook endpoint for you, it just received a signed `charge.paid` event.

## Payment links

**Payment links → Create a payment link** makes one shareable link; each customer who opens it gets
their own charge. Its id is saved automatically, so **Retrieve** and **Deactivate** work right after.

## Run everything at once

Click the collection → **Run** → **Run FirstFlip API (v1)**. Every request checks its own status,
so you see green or red per step.

## When something fails

Open **Console** (bottom left). Failed requests log the FirstFlip error code, for example
`amount_too_small` or `invalid_api_key`. Every code is explained in the docs:
guides/idempotency-and-errors.md in the FirstFlip developer docs.

- **401 invalid_api_key**: the key is wrong, revoked, or still `ffk_test_REPLACE_ME`.
- **404 not_found on every request**: the Developer API isn't switched on yet.
- **403 live_mode_unavailable**: you used a live key; live mode isn't open yet.

Generated from openapi.yaml; don't edit by hand.
